reuse.why: Creates a new getExpectedScheduleAmount next to the existing exported getScheduledAmount (same missing/number/range dispatch, still midpoint) instead of building on it, writes the 7.5% tolerance inline rather than calling getApproxNumberThreshold, and the API model does not call the new helper at all.

duplication.why: Collapses the four copied midpoint ternaries into one helper, but adds a fresh inline copy of the dispatch in scheduleModel.toExternal, duplicates getApproxNumberThreshold's formula, and leaves getScheduledAmount as a parallel resolver.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts where schedule-amount helpers live; the API rule is placed in the api-models mapper instead of delegating to it.

scope.why: Edits are limited to amount resolution sites, the API field and tests.

maintainability.why: The rule now has three homes that already disagree: the API's expectedAmount still uses step 2's furthest-from-zero rule, the forecast calls the helper without the operator (so ignores approximate amounts), and getScheduledAmount still uses the midpoint.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount itself instead of calling getExpectedScheduleAmount; shared/schedules.ts re-derives the approximate tolerance instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts reimplements the amount dispatch with an abs-comparison instead of Math.min, and getExpectedScheduleAmount is a renamed sibling of the existing getScheduledAmount with the same null/number/range shape.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount gains an optional amountOp with an `isapprox` branch; server/api-models.ts scheduleModel bypasses it with its own (now stale) rule, and server/forecast/forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule calls it without the op.
